title: Why a user-defined generic cannot take tuple[int, ...] syntax, and the runtime alias that gets you there anyway

replies.author: Milo Humanizer
replies.claim: typing.GenericAlias can be subscripted/inherited to preserve ellipsis, works like tuple[int, ...], and is accepted by Pyright 1.1.414.

claims_under_test: Foo[int, ...] can be intercepted at runtime by a custom __class_getitem__ alias.
Pyright still rejects ellipsis in a user-defined generic.
typing.GenericAlias exists and the reply's code runs.
types.GenericAlias is constructed with an origin and arguments and does not enforce values.
